evidence.claim: Desert and farmland on the approach to Great Basin National Park
evidence.quote: The highway comes upon the town of Baker, near which there are pockets of farmland. In Baker, the route intersects Lehman Caves Road (SR 488), which is the gateway to Great Basin National Park.

evidence.claim: Baker Road runs northwest from the Utah line through desert, passing pockets of farmland near Baker before continuing to US 6 and US 50.
evidence.quote: From there, the route heads northwesterly on Baker Road through the desert terrain. The highway comes upon the town of Baker, near which there are pockets of farmland.

evidence.claim: The Nevada Department of Transportation designated it a Nevada Scenic Byway in 2000, together with adjoining SR 488 and a portion of US 6/US 50.
evidence.quote: The Nevada Department of Transportation designated State Route 487 as a Nevada Scenic Byway on March 27, 2000, simultaneously with SR 488 and the portion of US 6/US 50 near the highway's northern terminus.

evidence.claim: The National Park Service describes the country near Great Basin National Park as extremely remote, with limited services and little to no cell coverage.
evidence.quote: Great Basin National Park is located in extremely remote, east-central Nevada, five miles west of the town of Baker. This is a remote area with limited services, little to no cell coverage

evidence.claim: Baker Road appeared on official Nevada highway maps by 1937, carrying the number SR 73 on some maps.
evidence.quote: Baker Road first appears on official Nevada state highway maps as far back as 1937. Although the state's tourist maps did not show Baker Road carrying the State Route 73 designation until 1942, other state maps show the route number existing on the highway by 1937.

evidence.claim: It was gravel by 1948 and fully paved by 1949.
evidence.quote: The route was upgraded to a gravel road by 1948, and was fully paved by 1949.

evidence.claim: Nevada’s statewide renumbering assigned it SR 487 in 1976; the change reached the official highway map’s 1978–79 edition.
evidence.quote: The State Route 487 designation was assigned to the former alignment of SR 73 on July 1, 1976. The resulting change in the highway number was first seen on the 1978–79 edition of the official highway map.

evidence.claim: Coming north through Garrison, Utah 21 becomes Nevada 487 at the state line, where travelers enter Pacific time.
evidence.quote: Travel north on Utah State Highway 21 through Milford, UT and Garrison, UT, which will become Nevada State Highway 487 as you cross the border.

evidence.claim: In Baker, Highway 488 branches west for the five-mile approach to the park.
evidence.quote: In Baker, turn west on Highway 488 and travel five miles to reach the park.

evidence.claim: Baker Road itself continues northwest through desert to its junction with US 6/US 50.
evidence.quote: Leaving the town, SR 487 continues northwesterly through more desert lands. The route ends at the intersection of US 6/US 50

evidence.claim: Baker’s connection to public land predates the national park.
evidence.quote: Baker Ranger Station was established in 1911 at the edge of Baker, Nevada to administer U.S. government lands in White Pine County, Nevada.

evidence.claim: A ranger station opened at the town’s edge in 1911 to administer federal land in White Pine County.
evidence.quote: Baker Ranger Station was established in 1911 at the edge of Baker, Nevada to administer U.S. government lands in White Pine County, Nevada.

evidence.claim: Its original four-room building was removed before construction of a new group began with a cottage in 1935.
evidence.quote: The first Baker Ranger Station was built in 1911, amounting to four rooms and regarded as unsightly. It was removed by the time new structures were built, beginning with a 1935 cottage

evidence.claim: The station transferred to the National Park Service in 1986 as an administrative center for Great Basin National Park.
evidence.quote: In 1986 Great Basin National Park was established and the station was transferred to the National Park Service as an administrative center for the park.

evidence.claim: Baker stands at the junction of routes 487 and 488, five miles east of the park’s main entrance.
evidence.quote: It is located 5 miles (8.0 km) east of the main entrance of Great Basin National Park at the junction of State Routes 487 and 488.

evidence.claim: Lehman Caves received federal protection before the surrounding mountain landscape became a national park.
evidence.quote: President Warren G. Harding created Lehman Caves National Monument by presidential proclamation on January 24, 1922. The monument and its surroundings was designated a national park on October 27, 1986

evidence.claim: President Warren G. Harding proclaimed the caves a national monument in 1922; the park designation followed in 1986 after advocacy by Congressman Harry Reid.
evidence.quote: President Warren G. Harding created Lehman Caves National Monument by presidential proclamation on January 24, 1922. The monument and its surroundings was designated a national park on October 27, 1986, following the advocacy of Congressman Harry Reid.

evidence.claim: The park includes ancient bristlecone pine groves and Wheeler Peak, which rises to 13,063 feet.

evidence.claim: Vegetation changes with elevation: sagebrush and Utah juniper grow near the visitor center, while higher country supports mountain meadows, quaking aspen and Engelmann spruce.
evidence.quote: The area around the Visitor Center is dominated by plants such as sagebrush, saltbush, single-leaf pinyon, and Utah juniper. Higher elevations are home to mountain meadows, white fir, quaking aspen, Engelmann spruce
